Coffee_Tea_Bags.title: How to Properly Recycle Coffee & Tea Bags
steps: Collect used coffee grounds and tea bags after brewing.
Check if tea bags contain synthetic materials; prefer compostable ones.
Remove any staples or plastic parts from tea bags.
Add coffee grounds and tea bags to your home compost bin or local composting facility.
Use composted material as fertilizer for plants.
Encourage others to compost coffee and tea waste instead of throwing it in the trash.
Spread awareness about reducing packaging waste by using loose leaf tea or bulk coffee.
precautions: Do not compost tea bags that contain plastic components.
Avoid composting excessive amounts of coffee or tea waste at once to maintain compost health.
Do not use compost from non-compostable tea bags.
Store waste in a dry container before composting to prevent mold.
Do not throw coffee grounds directly into storm drains.

Egg_Shells.title: How to Properly Recycle Egg Shells
steps: Collect clean eggshells after use.
Rinse to remove egg residue and let them dry.
Crush the eggshells into small pieces for faster decomposition.
Add crushed eggshells to your compost bin or home garden soil.
Eggshells enrich the compost with calcium and improve soil structure.
Encourage others to compost eggshells instead of throwing them in regular trash.
Spread awareness of the benefits of eggshell composting.
precautions: Do not compost large quantities at once to avoid imbalance.
Ensure eggshells are clean and dry before composting.
Avoid adding eggshells with raw egg residue to prevent attracting pests.
Do not throw eggshells in plastic waste bins.
Do not burn eggshells.

Food_Scraps.title: How to Properly Recycle Food Scraps
steps: Collect vegetable peels, fruit scraps, leftover food, and bread crumbs.
Separate food scraps from non-compostable waste like plastics and metals.
Use a home compost bin or local composting service for food waste.
Avoid composting meat, dairy, or oily food unless your system supports it.
Composted food scraps turn into nutrient-rich fertilizer for plants and soil.
Educate family and neighbors about reducing food waste through composting.
Spread awareness on preventing food waste and its environmental impact.
precautions: Do not compost meat, dairy, or greasy food in home compost (unless certified for composting).
Store food scraps in a sealed container to prevent odors.
Avoid mixing food scraps with recyclables.
Do not burn food waste.
Do not throw food scraps in plastic bags or landfill bins.

Kitchen_Waste.title: How to Properly Recycle Kitchen Waste
steps: Collect peelings, trimmings, coffee grounds, eggshells, and leftover vegetable matter.
Separate biodegradable kitchen waste from plastics and metals.
Use a compost bin or municipal composting facility.
Ensure waste is free from plastic or non-biodegradable items.
Compost kitchen waste into rich organic matter for gardens.
Share this process with family and neighbors to promote sustainable disposal.
Advocate for responsible kitchen waste disposal.
precautions: Do not compost oils, fats, or dairy unless specifically allowed.
Do not use plastic bags in compost bins.
Store waste in covered containers to prevent pests.
Do not burn kitchen waste.
Keep kitchen waste away from children and pets.

Yard_Trimmings.title: How to Properly Recycle Yard Trimmings
steps: Collect leaves, grass clippings, small branches, and plant trimmings.
Separate yard trimmings from plastics, metals, and hazardous waste.
Use home composting or municipal green waste collection services.
Chop large branches into smaller pieces for easier composting.
Avoid composting diseased plants or invasive weeds.
Use composted yard trimmings to enrich garden soil or as mulch.
Promote sustainable yard waste disposal practices.
precautions: Do not compost chemically treated plants or diseased plant matter.
Avoid composting large wood chunks without proper processing.
Do not mix yard trimmings with regular garbage.
Do not burn yard waste as it can release harmful smoke.
Store trimmings properly to prevent pest attraction.
